query: By how much did the FOMC cut rates at the September 18, 2024 meeting, and what is the new target range?
reference_answer: At the September 18, 2024 meeting, the Committee lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by a half percentage point (50 basis points), to 4.75-5.00 percent.
gold_transcript_excerpt: at today's meeting the committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by a half percentage point to four four and three quarters percent to five percent

query: What was headline PCE and core PCE inflation over the 12 months ending August 2024, per Chair Powell?
reference_answer: Total PCE prices rose 2.2 percent over the 12 months ending in August 2024, and core PCE prices (excluding food and energy) rose 2.7 percent.
gold_transcript_excerpt: total PCE prices rose 2.2 percent over the 12 months ending in August, and that excluding the volatile and energy categories, core PCE prices rose 2.7 percent

query: What was the U.S. unemployment rate as of the September 2024 press conference, according to Chair Powell?
reference_answer: The unemployment rate had moved up but remained low at 4.2 percent.
gold_transcript_excerpt: The unemployment rate has moved up but remains low at 4.2 percent.

query: What did Chair Powell say inflation had eased from and to, at the start of his September 2024 remarks?
reference_answer: Powell said inflation had eased substantially from a peak of 7 percent to an estimated 2.2 percent as of August 2024.
gold_transcript_excerpt: Inflation has eased substantially from a peak of 7 percent to an estimated 2.2 percent as of August.

query: What was average monthly payroll job growth over the three months before the September 2024 FOMC meeting?
reference_answer: Payroll job gains averaged 116,000 per month over the three months before the meeting, a notable step down from the pace seen earlier in the year.
gold_transcript_excerpt: Payroll job gains averaged $116,000 per month over the past three months, a notable step down from the pace seen earlier in the year.

query: According to the September 2024 SEP, where does the median FOMC participant project the federal funds rate at the end of 2024 and end of 2025?
reference_answer: The median participant projected the federal funds rate would be 4.4 percent at the end of 2024 and 3.4 percent at the end of 2025.
gold_transcript_excerpt: the median participant projects that the appropriate level of the federal funds rate will be 4.4 percent at the end of this year and 3.4 percent at the end of 2025

query: How many of the 19 SEP participants wrote down multiple rate cuts for 2024, per Chair Powell's Q&A remarks?
reference_answer: All 19 participants wrote down multiple cuts for 2024; 17 of the 19 wrote down three or more cuts, and 10 of the 19 wrote down four or more cuts.
gold_transcript_excerpt: all 19 of the participants wrote down multiple cuts this year all 19... 17 of the 19 wrote down three or more cuts and 10 of the 19 wrote down four more cuts

query: What was the median SEP projection for total PCE inflation for the current year and next year, per Chair Powell's September 2024 remarks?
reference_answer: The median SEP projection for total PCE inflation was 2.3 percent for the current year (2024) and 2.1 percent for next year (2025).
gold_transcript_excerpt: The median projection in the SEP for total PCE inflation is 2.3 percent this year and 2.1 percent next year, somewhat lower than projected in June.

query: What GDP growth rate did Powell cite for the first half of 2024?
reference_answer: GDP rose at an annual rate of 2.2 percent in the first half of 2024, with available data pointing to a roughly similar pace of growth for the current quarter.
gold_transcript_excerpt: GDP rose at an annual rate of 2.2 percent in the first half of the year, and available data point to a roughly similar pace of growth this quarter.

query: What did Powell say about the ratio of job vacancies to unemployed workers at this press conference?
reference_answer: Powell said the ratio of job vacancies to unemployed workers had come down from a peak of about two vacancies per unemployed person to around one, which he described as still a very good number.
gold_transcript_excerpt: that number reached two to one two vacancies for every unemployed person as measured it's now below around it's around one but that's still that's still a very good number

query: How did Powell compare the policy stance adopted in July 2023 to labor market and inflation conditions at the September 2024 meeting?
reference_answer: Powell noted the policy stance adopted in July 2023 came when unemployment was 3.5 percent and inflation was 4.2 percent; by the September 2024 meeting, unemployment had risen to 4.2 percent while inflation had fallen to a few tenths above 2 percent, which he said meant it was time to recalibrate policy.
gold_transcript_excerpt: the policy stance we adopted in july of 2023 came at a time when unemployment was three and a half percent and inflation was 4.2 percent today unemployment is up to 4.2 percent inflation's down to a few tenths above two

query: What did Powell say when asked whether the size of the September 2024 rate cut meant the Fed was 'behind' on policy?
reference_answer: Powell said he did not think the Committee was behind, calling the half-point cut timely and a sign of the Fed's commitment not to fall behind.
gold_transcript_excerpt: I would say we don't think we're behind. We do not think we're behind. We think this is timely.

query: What did Chair Powell say about the pace of future rate cuts after the September 2024 half-point cut?
reference_answer: Powell said the Committee would proceed carefully, meeting by meeting, cautioning that no one should view the half-point cut as the new pace of cuts going forward.
gold_transcript_excerpt: I think we're going to go carefully, meeting by meeting, and make our decisions as we go.

query: What did Powell say about the Fed's balance sheet runoff continuing alongside the September 2024 rate cut?
reference_answer: Powell said reserves remained abundant and were expected to stay so for some time, and that balance sheet runoff and rate cuts could happen side by side since both are forms of policy normalization -- there was no plan to stop the runoff because of the rate cut.
gold_transcript_excerpt: reserves are still abundant and expected to remain for some time... we're not thinking about stopping runoff because of this at all... for a time you can have the balance sheet shrinking but also be cutting rates
